test_policy.notes: Domestic freshmen with a minimum 3.5 weighted HS GPA may choose not to submit SAT/ACT (test optional; not a guarantee of admission, and a challenging curriculum plus leadership/work/service evidence is expected). The international FAQ says SAT/ACT is NOT required of international applicants, except those from an English-speaking exempt country or with 2+ years at a U.S. high school. The international merit-award table lists SAT/ACT or TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo thresholds, and the merit page says SAT/ACT scores are considered only for applicants who do not apply test optional.

requirements.notes: Apply on Coastal's own application or the Common App. The fee is not stated consistently: the international freshman page and the CDS say $45, while the freshman application pages say $60, so it is left blank. Also required: at least 3 years of official secondary transcripts or national exam results (original language plus official English translation) emailed to internationaladmissions@coastal.edu, and a copy of a valid passport (no decision is made without it). The Confidential Financial Statement and bank documents are needed before the I-20, not for the admission decision. Test-optional applicants may be asked for recommendation letters and an essay or personal statement.

deadlines.notes: Apply Oct. 15, know Dec. 1, enroll by Jan. 15 (years not printed; treated as the 2026-27 cycle). Listed on the freshman application page; the international pages do not mention ED or EA.

deadlines.label: Early Action (non-binding), fall 2027 entry (domestic freshman page; international pages list rolling admission only)
deadlines.notes: Apply Nov. 15, know Dec. 15, reply by May 1.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision, fall 2027 entry (domestic freshman page; international pages list rolling admission only)
deadlines.notes: Apply Feb. 1, know Mar. 1, reply by May 1. The merit-award page says funding is limited after these priority dates.

deadlines.label: International fall applicants: recommended completion date
deadlines.notes: The international FAQ says Coastal has rolling admission (space permitting) and recommends complete fall applications by June 1 (spring Nov. 1, summer May 1). The international merit page uses June 1 as its fall priority date. Printed without a year; treated as fall 2027.

english_policy.waiver_notes: No extra English proof is needed from citizens of listed English-speaking countries (e.g. UK, Ireland, Canada except Quebec, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Philippines, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Jamaica); those applicants and anyone with 2+ years of U.S. or English-speaking-country high school must instead submit SAT or ACT. Other ways to show proficiency: SAT EBRW 550 with combined 1070, ACT English and Reading 21 with composite 21, IB English A grade 5+, Cambridge AS/A level English, CAE/CPE at C1 or higher, GCSE/O-level English C or higher, TOEIC 645, GTEC 1140, MET/MELAB 74, ELS Level 110 (undergraduate), or 2 years at a U.S. high school with a B average in English. Scores must be within 2 years of the application date. Conditional admission (one year to submit English proof) is offered only to applicants who do not need an F-1/J-1 visa. The Global Achievement Pathway (English support plus coursework) is currently not offered.

aid.notes: All international applicants are automatically considered for merit awards (no separate application) if admitted by the priority dates (June 1 fall for international applicants, or Oct. 15 / Nov. 15 / Feb. 1 for freshmen). International freshman awards per year: Presidential $19,662 (SAT 1390+/ACT 31+/TOEFL 110/IELTS 8.0/Duolingo 130 and an A average), President's $13,000 (1300+/28+/102/7.5/120, B+), Provost's $10,000 (1200+/25+/90/7.0/110, B+), Coastal Scholar $7,500 (SAT 1100+/ACT 22+/TOEFL 79/IELTS 6.5/Duolingo 105, B+), Teal Scholar $4,500 (SAT 1030+/ACT 20+/TOEFL 74/IELTS 6.5/Duolingo 100, B). Applicants applying test optional are not scored on SAT/ACT. Awards are renewable annually; funding historically runs out after the priority dates. Non-Resident Tuition Waivers (in-state rate, about $18,286 savings) are limited to the Sister-State Program (Rhineland-Palatinate, Thuringia, Brandenburg, Queensland, Taiwan) and a limited number for Aruba and Iceland. CDS H6: only non-need-based institutional aid for nonresidents; 78 recipients, average $27,105. International students are not eligible for federal aid.

cost.notes: From the international costs page (2026-27, fall and spring only): undergraduate out-of-state tuition and fees combined $31,301 (stored as tuition_intl_usd; in-state and separate fee amounts are not given for 2026-27); housing $7,830 + meals $4,728 = $12,558; books $1,342; other living expenses $4,534; estimated undergraduate cost of attendance $49,736. F-1/J-1 applicants must show funds at least equal to this total. The 2025-26 CDS figures are in the colleges file.
